prior_coverage: The repo has not swept this family before. A grep on 28.9 for garmin, connect iq, wear os, watch face, facer, zepp, amazfit, fitbit, galaxy store, samsung, pebble and rebble found no venue verdicts. Samsung appears only as a Playgama partner (research/breadth/scouts/html5-games.json:104). Four related findings stand. (1) Google Play is rejected at $25 plus identity plus 12 testers for 14 days (docs/REJECTED.md:1395-1396; docs/INCOME_PLAN.he.md:267). Samsung now routes Wear OS faces to Play, so this rejection applies to them. (2) Microsoft Store is DEAD on its selfie step (html5-games.json, Microsoft entry). (3) PayPal receiving works in Israel, with 18% VAT on fees (docs/INCOME_PLAN.he.md:95). This matters because KiezelPay, the only cross-watch payment rail found, pays out only through PayPal. (4) Constraint 8 (MISSION.md) hits the critic's home-turf asset directly. hebrew_date (products/mcp-il-tools/src/server.ts:86) is a thin wrapper over @hebcal/core (products/mcp-il-tools/src/israeli.ts:5,120-121), which is GPL-2.0 (node_modules/@hebcal/core/package.json 'license'). It is a public input, not a private one. At least four free MIT Garmin Hebrew-date, zmanim or Shabbat projects already exist on GitHub (Ariel-Gal/KodeshMode, Biswaspr1022/KodeshMode, Yossizz/garmin-hebrew-date, aldomanpi/garmin-hebrew-library). Whether they are listed in the store is unknown. So the Hebrew angle gives us an audience, not an edge. A paid face competes with free ones on design and polish. If hebcal code is shipped it must go out under GPL; the other route is a clean reimplementation of the calendar arithmetic. Family-level finding: no watch store here pays an Israeli seller natively. Garmin Pay needs $100 a year and a US, CA, AU, SG or EU entity. Zepp pays only certified mainland-China corporate developers. Samsung sends faces to Google Play. Every live path runs through KiezelPay (27%, minimum $0.27, PayPal-only payout, all snippet grade). KiezelPay's onboarding, country list and any camera step are still unread.

gate_zero_cost.evidence: The 2026 hobby release docs read (dottorblaster/pebtrader-zero docs/releasing.md; Skarian/pebble tools/pebble-watchface/SKILL.md) contain no fee step, only `pebble login` and `pebble publish`. gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: The store has no native paid path. A code search of pebble-dev/rebble-appstore-api for paid, price, kiezelpay or monetiz returns 0 hits. Money could come only through KiezelPay, which 'only offers payouts via PayPal ... every last Thursday of the month' to a verified PayPal account (snippet, kiezelpay.com/faq). PayPal works in Israel (docs/INCOME_PLAN.he.md:95, repo). Not established: KiezelPay's merchant onboarding, its countries, any ID or camera step, and whether it still supports Pebble in 2026. Its Pebble launch post dates from 2016 (pebble-dev/developer.rebble.io source/_posts/2016-04-06-KiezelPay.md).

gate_programmatic_listing.evidence: `pebble publish` creates and releases a new listing from the CLI. Flags: `--non-interactive` ('No prompts, use flags/defaults'), `--name` ('new apps only'), `--description` ('required for new non-interactive'), `--category`, `--is-published` ('Make release immediately visible'). Sources: Skarian/pebble tools/pebble-watchface/SKILL.md, and ThemeParks/pebble scripts/publish_dest.py, which uses `--non-interactive` 'for first-time app creation'. Caveat: login is a browser OAuth. Whether its token can move to a CI runner is UNKNOWN; if it cannot, every publish session needs a person at a browser.

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: No store content policy was read. Several 2026 repos that publish to this store carry agent skills for Pebble faces (e.g. .claude/skills/pebble-watchface/SKILL.md in ehjacobs/pebble-sky and asebrech/fdf-time). That shows AI-assisted faces are being published. It does not show the store's rules allow them or require a declaration.

gate_buyer_supply.evidence: The store is live and takes 2026 submissions (bastooky/kaleido, created 2026-07: 'On the Pebble appstore!'). saltedlolly/all-things-pebble says Core Devices runs apps.repebble.com with a dashboard at appstore-api.repebble.com/dashboard. No user, install or revenue numbers were read. With no native paid tier, a buyer exists only if a free install converts at the KiezelPay prompt.

candidates.discovery_needs_prior_sale: Not gated on sales, because the store has no sales to rank on; installs are free. How the store ranks (hearts, installs, recency) is UNKNOWN.
candidates.owner_step: (1) Run `pebble login` once, with a brand-owned Google/Firebase identity, in a browser. (2) Open a KiezelPay merchant account paid out to a verified PayPal. This step is shared with the Garmin, Zepp and Fitbit candidates.
candidates.estimate_basis: Inference only. No repo source or source read gives a revenue base rate for revived Pebble. The store has no paid tier and its user base is unmeasured. The platform's culture is free apps, and KiezelPay keeps 27% of a $2-3 unlock. The ₪100 high end is an order-of-magnitude placeholder, not a computed figure.
candidates.time_to_first_sale: About 1-2 months after the two owner steps, if any trial converts; plausibly never.

candidates.discovery_needs_prior_sale: Not gated on sales, but gated on install velocity: 'Rank responds to recent movement'. A new listing is 'visible in the store for maybe a week or two'. 'Browse depth is capped at four pages per category', and search is the fallback (verden11). Free trial installs build rank before any sale, so the cold start is possible but the window is short.
candidates.owner_step: (1) A Garmin developer account on a brand email. (2) A KiezelPay merchant account with a verified PayPal (shared). (3) One dashboard submission per new face or data field. Step 3 is the per-item owner click that fails the gate.
candidates.estimate_basis: Prices of €2.49–5.99 and the conversion ranges come from verden11 (github, secondary). KiezelPay keeps 27%. The only income datum for indie developers is an ~8-year-old forum line quoted there: 'don't expect more than a beer or so a month'. The niche is Hebrew/Jewish Garmin owners, with free MIT competitors. The ₪250 high end assumes a few hundred installs a month converting at a few percent. That install volume is an assumption, not a base rate.
candidates.time_to_first_sale: About 1-2 months after the owner steps. Review takes 24h to 10+ days with no SLA (verden11), plus the trial period.
